title: Connect an org and link a user
lede: {{castAdminName}} connects a Salesforce Developer org to PingOne Privilege, then links {{castAName}}. Every step is observed on one org and one Privilege build, UNVERIFIED as a product claim. Simulated; hosts are examples.

nodes.label: Salesforce org (mock): users and permission sets
Privilege users: {{castDupName1}} and {{castDupName2}} share an email

steps.title: Paste the org URL, generate the key
steps.what: The admin pastes any address from the org; Privilege converts it to the My Domain URL and generates a key and a certificate valid two years. The private key exists only in the wizard form: a refresh means a new key and a new certificate to upload.

steps.title: Create the External Client App
steps.what: In Salesforce the admin creates the app with JWT Bearer Flow and the certificate, the scopes api and refresh_token, Permitted Users set to pre-authorized, and a permission set linked to the app and assigned to the user Privilege signs in as. A new app can take up to 10 minutes to activate.

steps.title: Privilege signs in with a signed JWT
steps.what: Privilege signs in as one integration user with a signed JWT: no password, no consent screen. Miss any one of the three settings and Salesforce refuses with invalid_grant; each way it fails has a cause and a fix.

steps.title: The wizard shows Signed in
steps.what: The green line "Signed in to the org as the user" means the key, the certificate, the pre-authorization and the permission set link are all correct. Name the application and create it: Sync Status Ready.

steps.title: Sync reads users and permission sets
steps.what: Sync reads the org's users, profiles and permission sets. Privilege never creates a Salesforce user: someone without one waits until an admin creates it.

steps.title: The lists come back
steps.what: The Permissions list and the Salesforce users arrive; a permission set created in Salesforce shows up only after the next Sync.

steps.title: Link only on an identical email
steps.what: Privilege links a person only when the email is identical. {{castDupName1}} and {{castDupName2}} share one email, so neither links (its email matches 2 Privilege users); {{castAName}} has a unique email and links on the first Sync. A Federation ID did not override this in the one test run.
